body.heading: One basket, everything for tomorrow
paragraphs: The idea is borrowed from anyone who has ever packed a gym bag at night instead of at dawn: a single basket, box, or bag by the door that collects everything tomorrow needs. Library books, permission slips, sports kit, the form that needs a signature — in the basket, or it does not exist.
Fill it at a fixed moment, such as straight after dinner or as part of the bedtime routine. The trigger matters more than the container.

body.heading: Children run the checklist
paragraphs: A short picture list on the wall — bag, book, bottle, extras — lets a child check the basket themselves and call out what is missing while there is still time to find it. Being the checker is a better job than being the checked.
Grown-ups keep one item on their own list: look in the basket once, briefly, for the things only adults can fix, like forms and money. Then leave it alone.

body.heading: It will still fail sometimes
paragraphs: Something will be forgotten eventually — usually on the wettest day. Treat it as weather, not as a verdict on the system. A basket that works four mornings out of five has already paid for itself.
Keep a small spare kit in the car or at school if the system allows it — a spare sports top forgives many baskets. Forgiveness, planned in advance, is part of the design.

description: A single basket by the door, filled the night before and checked by the children themselves, ends most morning treasure hunts.
